chapter: La Rocca on who created jazz
title: La Rocca on Kepard, Oliver, carnival parades and funeral bands
summary: La Rocca says Black bands never played carnival parades, older players had to copy the ODJB rhythm, and funeral marches were not jazz.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Now, they say that this, but Freddie Kepit, they make a great big story about it, that he was asked by the Victor Company to record. He says he didn't want to record because he didn't want the world to know his stuff. But they didn't know that I knew all this stuff. They thought that I was just a dumb man, that I didn't know what was going on. They imported them all. The Kepits, the Olivers, and all of them, they all died in the gutter. None of them made good. None of them could make a record. They had to steal the rhythm pattern from the Dixieland Jazz Band and play with younger men to make a record, like Johnny Dodds and Louis Armstrong and the rest, who came after, long ways after. And that's how these old Negroes got by on it. And the legend is that they created this music in the district, in the carnival clubs. No Negro band has ever played, to my knowledge, in the carnival parades. They may have played since I went to New York for these little clubs like the 4th District Club, and the Buzzards and different other small organizations that parade on foot. They may have played there, but they never played no carnival parades, because I played them from 1908 till 1916, and no Negro bands ever played in them parades. Now they give you another laugh about, I see Souchon put out one time, about the burials, and they make so much of them. That is something that the white man had invented thousands of years ago, a military burial. In fact, I myself played many of these funerals. Jack Lane had many funerals he played for, that I was his leader, for the volunteer fire company of Gretna. And there are many note musicians played, these fleas of birds. Oh yeah. That was some of the tunes that we would play, coming to the graveyard, coming back we'd play ragtime music. There was no jazz in New Orleans.
